dissented.claim_defeated: there is no negation vocabulary because there is nothing to negate: a value opening with BUILT is not denying BUILT (contracts/status-claims.json, artifact_standing_rule)
dissented.finding: The biconditional is blind to every denial standing to the right of the rung, and it does not merely permit the wrong answer - it forbids the right one. With the entry declaring the leading rung, all of these pass with exit 0 and no defect: WITNESSED_RETRACTED, WITNESSED_CLAIM_WITHDRAWN, WITNESSED_NOT_REALLY, WITNESSED_BY_NOBODY, WITNESSED_FALSELY, RATIFIED_THEN_REVOKED, RATIFIED_NOT, RATIFIED_IN_ERROR_COUNTER_RECORDED, RATIFIED_PENDING_REVERSAL, BUILT_THEN_DELETED. RATIFIED_NOT is the sharpest single input: the value carries the token NOT as a denial, the entry declares RATIFIED, and the check reports no defect. Then the compulsion: declaring artifact_standing null on any of them earns STANDING_NOT_THE_LEADING_TOKEN. There is no admissible entry for RATIFIED_THEN_REVOKED other than one asserting RATIFIED.
dissented.consequence: The second witness diagnosis was that a guard is written against the reported instance rather than the class. The class is that the value denies the rung; the instances guarded were denials standing to the left of the rung. Removing the vocabulary removed the left-hand hole and left the right-hand one, and the biconditional then converts it from a permission into a requirement. Retraction is first-class in this repository - AGENTS.md says retraction adds a counter-record and never erases the original - so RATIFIED_THEN_COUNTER_RECORDED is an ordinary thing to write in a hand-written file, and the crosswalk would be required to type it RATIFIED. Unexploited today: no live value carries a denial after its leading rung, and the ten non-null standings are all BUILT led by BUILT.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: a refusal when the leading rung of a value is followed anywhere by a token the contract has not declared as an admissible continuation, so an unknown neighbour fails closed; or a declared modifier vocabulary in which the leading-rung reading is only available when every later token is known.

dissented.claim_defeated: tokens split on every non-alphanumeric run, so a hyphen cannot hide one (contracts/status-claims.json, artifact_standing_rule, and the tokens() docstring)
dissented.finding: Splitting on every non-alphanumeric run does not stop a negator hiding - it deletes any negator that is not ASCII alphanumeric, leaving the rung first. Every one of these passes with exit 0 while the entry declares the rung: -WITNESSED, !WITNESSED, ~WITNESSED, _WITNESSED, U+00AC WITNESSED, Cyrillic NE underscore WITNESSED, Cyrillic NET underscore WITNESSED, Greek OU underscore WITNESSED, and CJK U+975E underscore WITNESSED. A leading BOM (U+FEFF) before RATIFIED and a leading zero-width space (U+200B) before RATIFIED both assert RATIFIED. tokens(-WITNESSED) returns the single token WITNESSED and leading_standing returns WITNESSED.
dissented.consequence: This is the previous draft defect inverted rather than removed. The second draft could not see BUILT-NOT_WITNESSED because a non-underscore attached the negator to its neighbour; this draft cannot see -WITNESSED because a non-alphanumeric negator is discarded entirely before the first token is chosen. The ASCII members of the family are the ones that matter: -WITNESSED and !WITNESSED are plausible hand shorthand for not witnessed in a file the contract itself says is hand-written, and both are one keystroke. I checked the control direction and it holds: NOT-WITNESSED, with the negator spelled out, is correctly refused, because NOT survives as its own token. The break needs the negator itself to be non-alphanumeric. Unexploited today: all 48 live values are ASCII and none leads with punctuation.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: refusing any value carrying a byte outside the alphabet the contract declares for values - all 48 live values are ASCII uppercase, digits and underscore - so an unrecognised byte fails closed instead of vanishing; or choosing the leading token from the first run of the raw string rather than from a list that silently drops what precedes it.

dissented.claim_defeated: artifact_standing is the standing the value asserts (contracts/status-claims.json, artifact_standing_rule and derived_never_declared)
dissented.finding: The rule decides on word order, not on what the value says, and it is wrong in both directions on live data. Under-claiming: five live values state a standing plainly, the crosswalk now records null, and declaring the true standing is REFUSED with STANDING_NOT_THE_LEADING_TOKEN. node_identity_status carries PROPOSED_CONTRACT_BUILT_REGISTRY_READ_NO_ADMISSION_TRANSPORT; federation_crossing_status carries PROPOSED_CONTRACT_BUILT_SELF_TESTED_NO_TRANSPORT; public_projection_status carries PROPOSED_CONTRACT_BUILT_PUBLICATION_RECORDED_SEAT_SET; sov_operating_agent_status carries OWNER_ACCEPTED_CONTEXT_PROFILE_BUILT_SELF_TESTED_NOT_WITNESSED and, on its second line, RULED_ENVELOPE_STANDS_O17_BUILT_SELF_TESTED. Each says a contract or profile is BUILT. Each is typed as asserting no ladder position at all, and cannot be typed otherwise. Over-claiming, in the same breath: a value leading with a rung word used in another sense must declare that rung. OPEN_QUESTION_FOR_BDO, OPEN_SEAM_S20_UNRESOLVED, OPEN_TO_ANY_PARTICIPANT and OPEN_SOURCE_LICENCE_UNDECIDED all pass declaring standing OPEN, and declaring null on any of them is refused.
dissented.consequence: The token_trap section of the contract names exactly this hazard - PARTICIPANT_BINDING_OPEN carries OPEN about a binding rather than about the standing of the subject - and the new rule survives that one case only by the accident that OPEN sits last there. Move the same word to the front and the rule compels the false reading with no refusal available. Meanwhile the three entries the rule gets right for that reason (conformance_status, lessons_loop_status, ticket_metadata_reader_status) are right by word order rather than by meaning. Net on live data: of the eight entries carrying a rung token while declaring null, three are correct calls and five discard a standing the document really does carry. That is information the record held at 964f414 and does not hold at 7860b45.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: a derivation that reads the grammar of the value rather than its first word - a declared prefix vocabulary (PROPOSED_, OWNER_ACCEPTED_, RULED_) stripped before the standing question is asked, so PROPOSED_CONTRACT_BUILT_... yields BUILT and OPEN_QUESTION_... yields nothing; or, failing that, narrowing artifact_standing_rule prose to say it types the leading word and not the assertion, and recording the five as a known scope.

dissented.claim_defeated: an entry is a reading of the document, not a second place to assert something about it; every field an entry declares that can be derived is derived and compared, never trusted (contracts/status-claims.json, derived_never_declared) - and the design claim under test, that no entry can assert anything not derivable from the field name and the value string
dissented.finding: An entry can assert arbitrarily much, through three channels, and the check reports no defect. First, extra keys: SHAPE type-checks the five declared string keys and tests artifact_standing and reference for presence, and nothing anywhere rejects an eighth key. Adding any of these to a live entry passes with exit 0 - asserted_standing=RATIFIED, settled_by=seat:root, authority=GRANTED, reversible=false, witnessed_by=reports/observations/does-not-exist.json, and standing_source=READING, the very field this commit deleted. Second, detail: free prose, read only by the show subcommand, graded by nothing. Setting the detail of a live entry to the sentence this subject is RATIFIED by Bdo passes with exit 0. Third, reference: graded only where the value carries OWNER_ACCEPTED_A followed by a digit, or where the reference itself matches the packet pattern. Setting the reference of a live entry to decisions/9999-does-not-exist.md or to acceptance/accepted/A99.json passes with exit 0.
dissented.consequence: The design claim I was asked to attack is false as written, and the derived_never_declared sentence overstates what the code does. It is true of exactly three fields - subject, claim_kind and artifact_standing - and the entry has seven fields and an unbounded number of possible extra ones. The sharpest form is that standing_source can be put straight back and the checker will not notice: the only guard against the removed field is scripts/tests/test_status_claims.py test_no_entry_carries_a_removed_field, which lives in the tooling shard, not in the check verify.py runs under the name status claims are typed. A guard for the gate, sitting outside the gate, is the shape of defect this table exists to refuse.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: refusing any entry key outside the declared seven, which is one set difference in malformed(); plus either grading detail and reference or removing them from the entry, since a field the contract calls load-bearing and grades nowhere is a declaration by the standard of the table itself.

dissented.claim_defeated: LOOSE is deliberately far looser than FIELD: anything key-shaped whose name ends in status, quoted or not, hyphenated or not, in any case, with or without a space before the colon (scripts/sov_status_claims.py, LOOSE comment)
dissented.finding: It is not anything key-shaped; it is the six shapes two witnesses reported, and it now also cries wolf. Invisible to BOTH readers, earning neither FIELD_UNTYPED nor FIELD_UNREADABLE, each confirmed against an empty crosswalk with exit 0: a YAML list item, dash space byom_status colon OPEN, indented or not; a dotted key, node.v1_status colon OPEN and v1.status colon OPEN; a slashed key, services/asset_status colon OPEN; a flow mapping, brace byom_status colon OPEN brace; an anchored key, ampersand anch byom_status colon OPEN; a tagged key, bang bang str byom_status colon OPEN; a bracketed key; a backticked key; a key containing a space, my status colon OPEN and byom service_status colon OPEN; a colon inside the key, a:b_status colon OPEN; a plus in the key; and a full-width Latin s inside the key. Fifteen of the seventeen shapes I tried are invisible. In the other direction the detector now produces false positives on legitimate YAML: any nested status key at any depth earns FIELD_UNREADABLE, as do a nested build_status, a nested ci-status, a quoted nested status, an uppercase STATUS colon FOUNDING, and a top-level bare status colon FOUNDING.
dissented.consequence: This is the third consecutive commit in which this guard is written against the instances the previous witness happened to name. The list-item shape is not exotic - it is one of the two ways YAML expresses a sequence - and this file already holds sequence-valued keys. The false-positive direction is worse than noise, because a bare status colon FOUNDING is unrepairable inside the crosswalk: FIELD requires at least one character before the _status suffix, so read_fields cannot produce that pair, no entry can match it, and the only repair is editing STATUS.yaml - which the not_in_scope section of this very contract forbids, stating that the file is unchanged by this contract. A detector that can refuse a line the contract has promised not to fix has no admissible exit. Unexploited today: the live file carries zero lines of any of these shapes, in either direction.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: grading read_fields against a YAML parse of the same bytes and refusing any disagreement other than the eight known duplicate keys, which measures the scope of the reader instead of guessing it; or a LOOSE pattern matching any line whose text before the first colon contains the case-insensitive substring status, so the strict reader must justify every exclusion, paired with an explicit allow-list for nested keys.

dissented.claim_defeated: the committed contract describes the rule the committed code applies
dissented.finding: contracts/status-claims.json contradicts itself about its own standing rule, and two of its three descriptions are the rule of the previous draft. artifact_standing_rule states the new rule correctly. But token_trap, unedited in this commit, still reads: Tokens are compared whole and a token preceded by NOT is a denial ... which is why a token is honoured only where the entry declares standing_source: TOKEN, and why an entry whose value begins with a ladder word may not declare anything else. And derived_never_declared still reads: artifact_standing must be a whole undenied token of the value. Neither is true of this commit. The NOT-denial rule was deleted from the code; the string standing_source appears nowhere in scripts/sovstatus/refusals.py, nowhere in scripts/sov_status_claims.py, and on no crosswalk entry - I checked all 48 key sets and they are identical and seven-membered. The only surviving occurrence of standing_source in the whole contract is this stale sentence, presenting it as the live mechanism.
dissented.consequence: A launched agent reading this contract to learn how standing is typed is told the mechanism the second witness already walked through, and is told a field exists that does not. Nothing under scripts/ grades contract prose against contract behaviour, so this passes silently and no verify check moved. It matters more here than it usually would, because the whole argument of artifact_standing_rule is that the previous rule was wrong, and the file still carries the previous rule two keys away as if it were current.
dissented.what_would_have_defeated_this_finding: editing token_trap and derived_never_declared in the same commit that changed the rule; or a check refusing a contract that names a field no entry carries and no module reads, which is the same measurement TW-B4 asks for, run in the other direction.

residuals.finding: The reader still disagrees with itself about separators, which is the surviving half of SW-B2. expected_kind now upper-cases, so the letter-case half is genuinely repaired: ruled_open_until_bdo and owner_accepted_a2_packet now type correctly. But expected_kind matches the literal prefixes RULED_ and OWNER_ACCEPTED_A followed by a digit, while tokens() splits on every non-alphanumeric run. So within one entry the standing question is separator-insensitive and the kind question is not. These all pass with exit 0 typed as STATUS - reversible true, settled_by null - when they are rulings or acceptances: RULED-O19, RULED.O19, RULED-OPEN_UNTIL_BDO, a bare RULED, OWNER-ACCEPTED-A2_PACKET, OWNER_ACCEPTED-A2 and OWNER_ACCEPTED_A_2. The hyphenated acceptance form escapes the reference rule as well as the kind rule, because reference_contradicts uses the same regex to decide what packet the value carries. Minor rather than material because no live value is affected, and recorded because the module docstring makes separator-insensitivity its headline fix while applying it to only one of the two derivations.

The new refusal has two branches and the corpus proves one. I instrumented reference_contradicts and replayed all 12 corpus cases: branch one, where the value carries a packet id and the reference disagrees, fires in exactly one case; branch two, where the reference names a packet and the value carries none, fires in zero. Branch two is covered only by scripts/tests/test_status_claims.py, in the tooling shard. The corpus is what verify.py runs under the name status claim refusals fire and what selfcheck grades, so the check that exists to prove every refusal fires proves half of the newest one. AGENTS.md asks for a defeating case per consequential behaviour, and the bidirectional test inside selfcheck is by code name, which cannot see a branch.

The packet reference is compared to another declaration and never to the packet. reference_contradicts checks the packet id of the value against the packet id of the reference and stops. A value of OWNER_ACCEPTED_A999_X with reference A999 passes with exit 0 and no such packet exists; OWNER_ACCEPTED_A02_X with reference A02 passes self-consistently and the real file is A2.json. Meanwhile acceptance/accepted/A1.json through A5.json and acceptance/A6.json sit in the same worktree the check already reads, so this is a declaration graded where it could have been measured - the defect class the witnessing procedure names, appearing in the one refusal this commit added. Separately, PACKET_REFERENCE is anchored with dollar rather than backslash-Z, so a reference of A2 followed by a newline matches as A2; a trailing space is correctly refused. I checked the live data and it is truthful: A1 through A4 resolve to real packets, decisions/0034 and decisions/0042 resolve to real records, and the O-numbers and S19 are retired historical citations rather than paths.

The ladder is a declaration the checker reads and nothing validates. artifact_standing_ladder is taken from the contract at face value. Emptying it entirely and setting all 48 artifact_standing values to null passes with exit 0: the biconditional becomes vacuously satisfied and the whole standing rule switches off with no refusal, in the file the rule is written in. Nothing compares the ladder to CLASSIFICATION.md or SPEC.md, which own the vocabulary. Minor because the mutation is self-consistency-checked in the other direction - adding a word to the ladder forces every entry leading with it to declare it, so a partial edit is caught - and because editing the contract is a governed act. It is still the case that the alphabet of the oracle is supplied by the thing it grades.

Two live checks read the same bytes under two different rules. scripts/sov_standing.py claimed_standing reads the status fields of STATUS.yaml, splits on underscore only, takes the first ladder token found anywhere, and treats a preceding NOT as denial. scripts/sovstatus/refusals.py leading_standing reads the same fields and takes the first token only. Unicode probes that did NOT break anything, recorded so the negative result is available. No character in U+0020 through U+2FFF upper-cases into text that manufactures a rung or the RULED prefix; I enumerated them all. The Turkish dotless i and the dotted capital I, the sharp s which upper-cases to SS, the long s which upper-cases to S, and the fi ligature all either leave the derivation unchanged or make it fail closed: RULE followed by sharp s upper-cases to RULESS_X and types as STATUS rather than smuggling a RULING through. Full-width Latin letters are treated as separators and fail closed. Combining marks split a token and fail closed. The only dangerous Unicode direction I found is TW-B2, where a non-ASCII negator is discarded and the rung becomes first.

standing_supported: Supports OPEN to BUILT for the seven paths, and supports the narrower claim that the findings of both prior witnesses are repaired: all 19 demonstrated bypasses are refused with named codes and no tracebacks. It does not support BUILT to WITNESSED. The third draft answers the second witness diagnosis correctly in method and incompletely in reach. Removing the negation vocabulary is the right kind of move - it kills the whole NOT_YET, NEVER, AWAITING and hyphenated family at once rather than one word at a time, which no extension of a word list would have done. But the biconditional is a rule about the first word of a value, not about what the value asserts, and the contract prose claims the second. Three consequences, all measured: a denial standing to the right of the rung is invisible, and the false standing is compelled rather than merely permitted (TW-B1); a non-alphanumeric negator is deleted rather than seen, which is the previous defect inverted (TW-B2); and five live values that plainly state BUILT are now typed as asserting nothing, with the true standing refused (TW-B3). Separately the design claim I was asked to attack is false as written: an entry can carry any extra key with no refusal, so the deleted standing_source can be put straight back, and detail and reference remain ungraded assertion channels (TW-B4). The scope guard of the reader is for the third time written against the reported instances, and now also refuses legitimate nested keys with no admissible repair (TW-B5). And the contract still carries the rule of the previous draft in two of its three descriptions, naming a field that no longer exists (TW-B6). None of the six is exploited by the committed data. All six are one hand edit away, in a file the contract itself says is hand-written.

judgement_items.question: The standing rule now decides on word order. It compels artifact_standing OPEN for a hypothetical OPEN_QUESTION_FOR_BDO and refuses artifact_standing BUILT for the live PROPOSED_CONTRACT_BUILT_SELF_TESTED_NO_TRANSPORT, so five live values that state a standing are recorded as stating none. Is a crosswalk that under-reads the record in five places preferable to one that could over-read it in none, or should the derivation strip a declared prefix vocabulary - PROPOSED_, OWNER_ACCEPTED_, RULED_ - before asking the standing question?

Three drafts have now each closed the instances a witness named and left the class open in a new spelling - first prose sources, then a NOT vocabulary, now word order and non-alphanumeric bytes. Each repair was correct and each was reachable by the next reader. Is a fourth repair cycle inside this concern the right move, or is the recurrence evidence that the derivation needs a fail-closed default, refusing any value whose every token is not accounted for by a declared vocabulary, so that an unrecognised input refuses instead of being read as an assertion?

The derived_never_declared section says an entry is a reading of the document and not a second place to assert something about it, and an entry can currently carry any additional key, arbitrary prose in detail, and an unresolvable reference, all with exit 0. Closing the extra-key half is one set difference in malformed(). Closing detail and reference means either grading them against the filesystem - the acceptance packets and decision records are already in the tree - or removing them from the entry. Which does Bdo want, given that the packets exist and the check already has the worktree open?

This is the third witness reading and the third to record that the commit cannot be landed consistently by the grant that would land it: registering two checks moves the record to 42, CLAUDE.md line 105 says 40, and CLAUDE.md is excluded from grant:standing-landing-loop as a root governing document. The contract now also declares itself witnessed by two observation files that are likewise not in the tree. Should the landing grant widen to cover a mechanical count on the orientation page, should the verification-checks claim of the snapshot read HEAD rather than the working tree, or should any check-registering change route to Bdo by construction?
